walkthroughs.body_html:
Ecosystems & Ecology — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ecosystems & Ecology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ecosystems & Ecology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Bacteria converting ammonium to nitrate in soil:
options: Rhizobium
Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter
Pseudomonas
E. coli

mcqs.q: Typical energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels:

options: How much an animal can physically carry.
The maximum population an environment can sustainably support given available resources.
Because plants only use carbon.
The size a species can reach.

mcqs.q: Why is atmospheric nitrogen unavailable to most plants directly?
options: Stopping all development immediately.
N2 has a strong triple bond that most organisms cannot break.
Because plants cannot reach high enough to access it.
Because plants only use carbon.

mcqs.q: How does the Brundtland Report define sustainable development?
options: Stopping all development immediately.
Environmental protection at all costs.
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.
The size a species can reach.
